pull.title: init: ignore repeated `-addnode` startup values
pull.body:
Startup `-addnode` values are copied directly into the connection manager's added-node list. Unlike runtime `addnode add` calls, this path does not reject repeated values.

For example:

```
-addnode=example.com
-addnode=example.com
```

Both entries are currently stored. While the destination is disconnected, `ThreadOpenAddedConnections()` processes
each entry during every retry cycle. 

This can cause redundant DNS lookups, connection attempts, and log messages. `getaddednodeinfo` also reports the repeated entry.

---

This change is complementary to, and independent of, #35600.

#35600 prevents overlapping manual connection attempts by tracking destinations while a connection attempt is in progress. 
This PR instead removes repeated `-addnode` values before the connection threads start, preventing duplicate stored entries and sequential redundant retries.

It does not replace or broaden #35600's in-flight connection handling.

I want to mention this explicitly, but I don't think it's really problematic, and I'm fine if it doesn't get fixed - we are changing how add checks for duplicates, but remove still compares exact strings. It means that one could do:
```
addnode abc.com add         # ok!
addnode abc.com:8333 add    # Error: Node already added
addnode abc.com:8333 remove # Error: Node could not be removed. It has not been added previously.
```

This is a bit confusing for the user - has `abc.com:8333` been added or not?

This is also present in master, it's not unique to this PR, since in master `add` already rejects numeric equivalents.

The fix would be to also check for equivalence in `RemoveAddedNode`.

events.message:
net: reject equivalent addnode host-port pairs

CConnman::AddNode rejects equivalent numeric addresses, but compares
unresolved hostnames as raw strings. As a result, the same hostname
with and without an explicit default port can be stored twice.

Compare the host text and effective port of values that SplitHostPort
can parse. Do not perform DNS resolution, and keep non-default ports
distinct.

Co-authored-by: Pablo Martin <pablomartin4btc@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Daniela Brozzoni <danielabrozzoni@protonmail.com>

net: match numeric aliases in AddedNodesContain

AddedNodesContain only matches an added node that is spelled exactly as
the address's canonical string. An equivalent numeric spelling, such as
an expanded IPv6 address or a bracketed IPv6 address without a port, is
never matched, so the automatic outbound logic can use a slot on that
peer. AddNode already rejects the canonical spelling as a duplicate of
such an entry, so it cannot be added alongside it.

Parse each added node as a numeric address and compare it with the
address. An entry without a port still matches the address at any port.
Parse after releasing m_added_nodes_mutex, as GetAddedNodeInfo does.

net: remove added nodes using the same equivalence as AddNode

CConnman::AddNode rejects a value that is equivalent to an existing
entry, but RemoveAddedNode only removes an exact string match. As a
result, `addnode <node> remove` can fail for a value that
`addnode <node> add` has just reported as already added.

Move the duplicate lookup into a FindAddedNode helper and use it in
both functions, so removal accepts any value that addition considers
a duplicate.

Co-authored-by: Daniela Brozzoni <danielabrozzoni@protonmail.com>

net: deduplicate startup -addnode values

Startup -addnode values are copied directly into CConnman state,
bypassing the duplicate checks used by the addnode RPC. Equivalent
values are consequently stored and retried independently.

Check each startup value with FindAddedNode, the lookup AddNode uses,
while holding m_added_nodes_mutex. Keep the first entry, and log each
ignored value together with the entry it matched, since equivalent
values can differ in port or numeric address spelling.

Co-authored-by: Daniela Brozzoni <danielabrozzoni@protonmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Pablo Martin <pablomartin4btc@gmail.com>

rpc: find equivalent added nodes in getaddednodeinfo

getaddednodeinfo only matches its node argument against the exact
string that was passed to addnode. A value that `addnode add` rejects
as already added, and that `addnode remove` accepts, is still reported
as not added.

Let GetAddedNodeInfo optionally return only the entry equivalent to a
node value, found with FindAddedNode under the same lock that takes the
snapshot, and use it in getaddednodeinfo.
doc: add release note for addnode equivalence

comments.body: minor nit: this logs only the rejected value, not what it matched against. For a user staring at their config wondering why an entry got dropped, "Ignoring duplicate -addnode value: node.example:8333 (matches node.example)" would be more actionable — especially since the whole point of this PR is catching non-obvious duplicates (different port representations), where "this is a duplicate" alone doesn't explain why. Not blocking, just a nice-to-have.

One more equivalence worth considering, in the same spirit as the host/port work here: hostname comparison is case-sensitive (`host == existing_host`), so `-addnode=Example.com` and `-addnode=example.com` wouldn't be caught as duplicates, since DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This isn't new — the original exact-string check had the same gap — and it's arguably out of scope for this PR. But since the whole point here is catching duplicate representations of the same target rather than just literal string matches, case-folding the hostname comparison feels like a natural extension of the same fix rather than a separate concern, so wanted to flag it while this code is already being touched. No test currently covers it either way, consistent with it not being handled. Happy to leave it out if you'd rather keep this PR narrowly scoped to the port-equivalence case.

comments.body: You should include a "\n" at the end of this sentence, otherwise the line in the logs for `Ignoring duplicate -addnode value: first.node:18444` will also match this one (`assert_debug_log` checks the presence of a substring). Currently, if you remove the duplicate `-addnode=first.node` line, the test still passes.
